name: downloads
title: Downloads
description: Your Downloads folder newest first (and the browsers' own download folders when they differ): size, kind or a thumbnail, age, sections by day, a download still coming in with its rate. Open, reveal, copy the file or its path, move to the Trash, move to a folder, rename; several at once; clear what is older than 30 days. The newest download of the last ten minutes sits in the root's Now section.
author: pal

store.tagline: Your downloads newest first: open, reveal, trash, tidy
features: ~/Downloads and the browsers' own download folders when they differ, newest first, sections Today, Yesterday, This week, Older; listed again on every show
Each row with its size, a kind glyph or a 64 px thumbnail (images and PDFs, cached) and its age; the detail pane shows the page it came from (Spotlight's `kMDItemWhereFroms`)
A download still coming in (`.crdownload`, `.part`, `.download`) leads the list under Downloading with its size growing as a rate, or Safari's own percentage
Enter opens, cmd+Enter reveals, cmd+c copies the file, cmd+shift+c its path, cmd+d moves to the Trash (asks first); Tab marks several for open, reveal, copy and trash
cmd+m moves a file to a folder and cmd+shift+r renames it, each through a form
Clear older than 30 days (the count and size in the row, asks first) and Open Downloads as the last rows; the newest download of the last ten minutes in the root's Now section

screenshots.caption: The folder newest first: a download coming in, then Today, Yesterday, This week, Older with sizes and ages
The detail pane: name, folder, size, kind, modified, and the page the file came from
What a download can do: open, reveal, copy, move, rename, trash
Move to folder: the form with the target
Three rows marked with shift+down (Tab marks too): open, reveal, copy or trash them at once
